{{Short description|Special constant related to the exponential integral}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Gompertz constant''' or '''Euler–Gompertz constant''',<ref name="Finch" /><ref name=":0">{{cite journal |last=Lagarias |first=Jeffrey C. |authorlink=Jeffrey Lagarias |year=2013 |title=Euler's constant: Euler's work and modern developments |journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]] |volume=50 |issue=4 |pages=527–628 |doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01423-X |doi-access=free|arxiv=1303.1856 }}</ref> denoted by <math>\delta</math>, appears in integral evaluations and as a value of [[special function]]s. It is named after [[Benjamin Gompertz]].

It can be defined via the [[exponential integral]] as:<ref>{{Cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |authorlink=Eric W. Weisstein |title=Gompertz Constant |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/GompertzConstant.html |access-date=1 August 2026 |website=[[MathWorld]]}}</ref>

:<math> \delta = -e\operatorname{Ei}(-1)=\int_0^\infty\frac{e^{-x}}{1+x}dx. </math>

The numerical value of <math>\delta</math> is about
:{{mvar|δ}} = {{val|0.596347362323194074341078499369}}... &nbsp; {{OEIS|id=A073003}}.

== History ==

When Euler studied divergent infinite series, he encountered <math>\delta</math> via, for example, the above integral representation. [[François Le Lionnais|Le Lionnais]] called <math>\delta</math> the Gompertz constant because of its role in [[Gompertz function|survival analysis]].<ref name="Finch" />

In 1962, Shidlovski proved that at least one of the [[Euler–Mascheroni constant]] and the Euler–Gompertz constant is [[Irrational number|irrational]].<ref name=Aptekarev2009>{{cite arXiv |last=Aptekarev |first=A. I. |date=2009 |title=On linear forms containing the Euler constant |class=math.NT |eprint=0902.1768}}</ref> This result was improved in 2012 by [[Tanguy Rivoal]], who proved that at least one of them is [[Transcendental number|transcendental]].<ref name=":0" /><ref name=Aptekarev2009 /><ref>{{cite journal |last=Rivoal |first=Tanguy |date=2012 |title=On the arithmetic nature of the values of the gamma function, Euler's constant, and Gompertz's constant |journal=[[Michigan Mathematical Journal]] |volume=61 |issue=2 |pages=239–254 |doi=10.1307/mmj/1339011525 |doi-access=free |authorlink=Tanguy Rivoal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Waldschmidt |first=Michel |authorlink=Michel Waldschmidt |date=2023 |title=On Euler's Constant |url=https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michel.waldschmidt/articles/pdf/EulerConstant.pdf |place=Sorbonne Université, Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu, Paris}}</ref>

==Identities involving the Gompertz constant==

The most frequent appearance of <math>\delta</math> is in the following integrals:
: <math> \delta = \int_0^\infty\ln(1+x)e^{-x}dx = \int_0^1\frac{1}{1-\ln(x)}dx</math>

which follow from the definition of {{mvar|δ}} by integration of parts and a variable substitution respectively.

Applying the Taylor expansion of <math>\operatorname{Ei}</math> we have the series representation

: <math> \delta = -e\left(\gamma+\sum_{n=1}^\infty\frac{(-1)^n}{n\cdot n!}\right). </math>

Gompertz's constant is connected to the [[Gregory coefficients]] via the following formula:<ref name='Mezo'>{{cite journal | last = Mező | first = István | title = Gompertz constant, Gregory coefficients and a series of the logarithm function | journal = Journal of Analysis and Number Theory | year = 2014 | volume = 2 | issue = 2 | pages = 33–36 | url = https://www.naturalspublishing.com/files/published/j18jp677r69ri8.pdf}}</ref>

: <math> \delta = \sum_{n=0}^\infty\frac{\ln(n+1)}{n!}-\sum_{n=0}^\infty C_{n+1}\{e\cdot n!\}-\frac{1}{2}. </math>
The Gompertz constant also happens to be the regularized value of the summation of alternating factorials of all natural numbers ([[1 − 1 + 2 − 6 + 24 − 120 + ⋯]]), which is defined by [[Borel summation]]:<ref name=":0" />
: <math> \delta = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} (-1)^k k!</math>
It is also related to several polynomial [[continued fraction]]s:<ref name="Finch" /><ref name=":0" />
: <math> \frac1\delta = 2-\cfrac{1^2}{4-\cfrac{2^2}{6-\cfrac{3^2}{8-\cfrac{4^2}{\ddots \cfrac{n^2}{2(n+1)-\dots}}}}}</math>
: <math> \frac1\delta = 1+\cfrac{1}{1+\cfrac{1}{1+\cfrac{2}{1+\cfrac{2}{1+\cfrac{3}{1+\cfrac{3}{1+\cfrac{4}{\dots}}}}}}}</math>
: <math> \frac{1}{1-\delta} = 3-\cfrac{2}{5-\cfrac{6}{7-\cfrac{12}{9-\cfrac{20}{\ddots \cfrac{n(n+1)}{2n+3-\dots}}}}}</math>
